passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Overview We design and manufacture semiconductors that we sell to electronics designers and manufacturers all over the world. Technology is the foundation of our company, but ultimately, our objective and the best metric for owners to measure our progress is through the growth of free cash flow per share over the long term. Our strategy to maximize long-term free cash flow per share growth has three elements: 1. A great business model that is focused on analog and embedded processing products and built around four sustainable competitive advantages. The four sustainable competitive advantages are powerful in combination and provide tangible benefits: (a) A strong foundation of manufacturing and technology that provides lower costs and greater control of our supply chain. (b) A broad portfolio of analog and embedded processing products that offers more opportunity per customer and more value for our investments. (c) The reach of our market channels that gives access to more customers and more of their design projects, leading to better insight and knowledge of customer needs and the opportunity to sell more of our products into each design. (d) Diversity and longevity of our products, markets and customer positions that provide less single point dependency and longer returns on our investments. Together, these competitive advantages help position TI in a unique class of companies capable of generating and returning significant amounts of cash for our owners. We make our investments with an eye towards long-term strengthening and leveraging of these advantages. 2. Discipline in allocating capital to the best opportunities. This spans how we select R&D projects, develop new capabilities, invest in manufacturing capacity or how we think about acquisitions and returning cash to our owners. 3. Efficiency, which means constantly striving for more output for every dollar spent. We believe that our business model with the combined effect of our four competitive advantages sets TI apart from our peers and will for a long time to come. We will invest to strengthen our competitive advantages, be disciplined in capital allocation and stay diligent in our pursuit of efficiencies. Finally, we will remain focused on the belief that long-term growth of free cash flow per share is the ultimate measure to generate value. For more information about market and business characteristics, see the Business discussion in Item 1 of this Form 10-K. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should read the following risk factors in conjunction with the factors discussed elsewhere in this and other of our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and in materials incorporated by reference into these filings. These risk factors are intended to highlight certain factors that may affect our financial condition and results of operations and are not meant to be an exhaustive discussion of risks that apply to TI, a company with broad international operations. Like many companies, we are susceptible to a potential downturn associated with macroeconomic weakness, which may affect our performance and the performance of our customers. Similarly, the price of our securities is subject to volatility due to fluctuations in general market conditions, actual financial results that do not meet our and/or the investment community’s expectations, changes in our and/or the investment community’s expectations for our future results, dividends or share repurchases, and other factors, many of which are beyond our control. Risks related to our business and industry Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions. We have facilities in more than 30 countries. About 60% of our revenue comes from customers with headquarter locations outside the United States. Revenue from end customers headquartered in China represented about 20% of our revenue in 2025, while revenue from products shipped into China represented about 50% of our revenue in 2025. We also continue to expand our offerings of online transactions and services worldwide. The semiconductor industry has recently been the focus of increased regulatory activity and scrutiny, which has contributed to variability in global trade conditions and supply chains. Certain countries where we operate, particularly the United States and China, have experienced, and other countries may experience, geopolitical tensions and administrative measures that affect global trade and macroeconomic conditions through the imposition of tariffs, including tariffs specific to the products that we sell, import or export restrictions, trade embargoes and sanctions, restrictions on cross-border investment and other trade barriers applicable to the semiconductor industry. Geopolitical tensions and administrative measures could limit our access to markets or impact our ability to deliver products, support customers, purchase or receive manufacturing equipment or materials, limit our suppliers’ and customers’ access to our products, or cause customers to seek alternate suppliers, which could adversely affect our operations and financial results. We are exposed to political, social and economic conditions, security risks, acts of war, terrorism or other hostile acts, pandemics, epidemics or other public health crises, labor conditions, climate change risks and possible disruptions in power, water supply, transportation, communications and information technology networks of the various countries in which we operate. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin sits well above the sector median, reflecting the analog and embedded processing model and manufacturing cost control. Profitability of this order funds interest and principal comfortably through the cycle, though the margin slipped modestly year over year as revenue recovered faster than operating income.

Interest coverage is strong and improved year over year, and EBITDA-based coverage also rose, placing the issuer at the sector median for interest coverage. Debt service is not a constraint at current earnings levels, and the cushion would absorb a meaningful earnings decline before coverage became a concern.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits modestly above the sector median even as it declined year over year, and net leverage on a cash-and-investments basis is roughly double the sector median. The indicative profile is minimal, but the peer gap means the balance sheet offers less relative headroom than headline coverage suggests.

The risk factors flag concentrated geographic exposure, with a large share of revenue tied to China end customers and shipments into China, alongside tariffs and export controls on semiconductors. Such measures could limit market access or push customers to alternate suppliers, pressuring revenue and cash flow that underpin the debt service profile.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow covers dividends and buybacks combined, but falls short of capital expenditure plus dividends, and free cash flow falls below total shareholder distributions. Capital intensity therefore competes directly with returns of capital for the same cash, leaving less retained buffer.

Free cash flow to debt improved year over year yet remains well below the sector median, and cash flow to debt also trails peers. Debt is entirely long-term with no commercial paper outstanding, so refinancing is not imminent, but the maturity schedule was not disclosed in the bundle, limiting assessment of near-term rollover needs.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, with leverage and cash flow both in the strongest tier and comfortable headroom to the next risk band. Liquidity is ample, with a current ratio far above the sector median, supporting the view that near-term obligations are well covered by liquid resources.

Our judgement is a solid investment-grade profile anchored by high margins and strong coverage, tempered by leverage above the sector median and free cash flow that does not fully fund distributions. Continued capital intensity and China-linked trade exposure are the main watch items rather than any imminent liquidity stress.

credit_strengths.text: 營業利潤率遠高於行業中位數，反映類比與嵌入式處理模式及製造成本控制。此等盈利水平足以在整個週期內輕鬆支付利息及本金，儘管利潤率按年溫和下滑，因收入復甦速度快於營業利潤。
利息覆蓋率強勁且按年改善，以EBITDA為基礎的覆蓋率亦上升，使發行人處於行業利息覆蓋率中位數。按目前盈利水平，償債並非限制，且緩衝足以吸收顯著的盈利下滑，才會令覆蓋率成為憂慮。

key_risks.text: 即使總槓桿按年下降，仍略高於行業中位數，而以現金及投資為基礎的淨槓桿約為行業中位數的兩倍。指示性狀況為極低，但同業差距意味著資產負債表提供的相對緩衝少於表面覆蓋率所顯示。
風險因素指出地理集中風險，大部分收入與中國終端客戶及付運至中國相關，同時面臨關稅及半導體出口管制。此等措施可能限制市場准入或促使客戶轉向替代供應商，對支撐償債狀況的收入及現金流構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流覆蓋股息及回購的總和，但不足以覆蓋資本開支加股息，而自由現金流低於股東分派總額。因此資本密集度直接與資本回報競爭同一現金，留下較少留存緩衝。
自由現金流對債務比率按年改善，但仍遠低於行業中位數，現金流對債務比率亦落後同業。債務全為長期，並無未償還商業票據，故再融資並非迫在眉睫，但資料包未披露到期時間表，限制了對短期滾動需求的評估。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，槓桿及現金流均處於最強級別，並與下一風險級別有舒適緩衝。流動性充裕，流動比率遠高於行業中位數，支持短期義務由流動資源充分覆蓋的觀點。
我們的判斷為穩健的投資級狀況，以高利潤率及強勁覆蓋率為錨，但受制於高於行業中位數的槓桿及未能完全支持分派的自由現金流。持續的資本密集度及與中國相關的貿易風險是主要關注事項，而非任何迫在眉睫的流動性壓力。
